title: Non-Coprime CRT: Beyond Standard CRT
content: When gcd(m,n) > 1, the natural map x ↦ (x mod m, x mod n) is no longer surjective onto ℤ/mℤ × ℤ/nℤ. This file characterizes the image: a pair (a,b) is reachable iff gcd(m,n) | (a-b). The proof uses Bézout coefficients (Int.gcdA, Int.gcdB) for the constructive direction and basic divisibility for the necessary condition. All 12 results are fully proved with 0 sorries.
mathContext: The generalized CRT: x ≡ a (mod m) ∧ x ≡ b (mod n) is solvable iff gcd(m,n) | (a-b). Solutions are unique mod lcm(m,n).

title: Forward Direction: Solvability Implies Divisibility
content: If x ≡ a (mod m) and x ≡ b (mod n), then gcd(m,n) | (a-b). The proof rewrites a-b = (a-x) - (b-x), then uses transitivity: gcd(m,n) | m | (a-x) and gcd(m,n) | n | (b-x), so gcd(m,n) divides the difference.
mathContext: This is the necessary condition for solvability. It follows from the fact that gcd(m,n) divides both m and n, hence any common residue must satisfy this constraint.

title: Backward Direction: Bézout Construction
content: Given gcd(m,n) | (a-b), constructs x = a - m·gcdA(m,n)·k where k = (a-b)/gcd(m,n). For the first congruence, m clearly divides a - x. For the second, the key step uses `linear_combination` with Bézout's identity gcd = m·gcdA + n·gcdB to show n divides b - x.
mathContext: This is the constructive heart of the theorem. Bézout coefficients provide the 'glue' that connects the two congruences. The `linear_combination` tactic automates the algebraic verification.

title: Uniqueness Modulo LCM
content: If x ≡ y (mod m) and x ≡ y (mod n), then x ≡ y (mod lcm(m,n)). The proof goes through natAbs: convert Int divisibility to Nat divisibility, apply Nat.lcm_dvd, then case-split on the sign of (y-x) via Int.natAbs_eq to convert back.
mathContext: In the coprime case, lcm(m,n) = mn recovers standard CRT uniqueness. For non-coprime moduli, lcm(m,n) < mn, giving a coarser but correct uniqueness modulus.

title: Explicit Solution Formula
content: genCRTSolution m n a b = a - m·gcdA(m,n)·((a-b)/gcd(m,n)). The first congruence holds unconditionally (m divides the correction term). The second congruence requires gcd(m,n) | (a-b) and uses the same linear_combination technique as the existence proof.
mathContext: This makes the generalized CRT constructive and algorithmic. Given any solvable system, this formula directly computes a solution without search.

title: Full Generalized CRT: Existence + Uniqueness
content: generalized_crt_full combines everything: given a ≡ b (mod gcd(m,n)), there exists x satisfying both congruences, and any two solutions are congruent mod lcm(m,n). The proof composes generalized_crt_modEq for existence with crt_unique_mod_lcm for uniqueness.
mathContext: This is the definitive statement of the non-coprime CRT. It packages existence (via Bézout) and uniqueness (via LCM) into a single theorem, ready for use in downstream formalizations.
